subject: Business Models
title: Media Rebundling
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Media Rebundling.

hook.text: Americans now spend more on streaming subscriptions than cable. The unbundled future costs more than the bundle.

buildup.text: Cord-cutters left cable for Netflix ($15), Hulu ($18), Disney+ ($14), HBO ($16), and more. It adds up fast.

discovery.text: Streaming started as cheaper than cable. But each service's content costs forced individual price hikes.

twist.text: Companies now sell bundles: Disney+/Hulu/ESPN+, Apple One, Amazon Prime Video in Prime. We've come full circle.

climax.text: The great unbundling of cable is becoming the great rebundling of streaming. Different pipes, same structure.

punchline.text: Left cable for cheaper streaming. Now streaming bundles cost more. Full circle.

quiz.question: What is happening in the streaming market now?
options: Services are rebundling into combined packages

details.summary: After cord-cutting unbundled cable TV into individual streaming services, the industry is now rebundling. Services offer combined packages, ad-supported tiers, and partnerships that increasingly resemble the cable bundle customers originally fled.
details.whyItMatters: Media rebundling demonstrates that unbundling creates its own problems. When consumers manage ten streaming subscriptions totaling more than cable, the convenience of a single bundle becomes attractive again, completing the cycle.
takeaways: Streaming services are combining into bundles resembling old cable packages
Subscription fatigue drives consumers back toward aggregated offerings
Ad-supported tiers recreate the cable TV advertising model at lower prices

faq.question: What rebundling trends are appearing in streaming?
faq.answer: Disney offers a combined Hulu-Disney-ESPN bundle. Apple and Amazon aggregate other services within their platforms. Carrier bundles include Netflix with phone plans. Aggregators like Roku offer channel packages. The trend toward re-aggregation is accelerating.

faq.question: Will streaming eventually look exactly like cable TV again?
faq.answer: Partially. Bundles will return in new forms, but with more consumer choice and on-demand flexibility. The key difference is that consumers can opt in and out monthly rather than being locked into annual contracts. The rebundle will be more flexible than cable was.
